land.text: Gascony, in personal union with Aquitaine 'from 660 to 769' (Duchy of Gascony page)

predecessors.note: The page dates the first duke to 602 ('Duke appointed by the Frankish kings: 602') and Odo and Waifer as dukes of Vasconia and Aquitaine; Cliopatria's Gascony row begins in 768 with the Carolingian takeover and Lop II, the 'probable founder of a Gascon line of dukes'.

land.text: Gascony, joined to Aquitaine when Gui-Geoffrey (William VIII), Duke of Gascony from 1052, became Duke of Aquitaine in 1058

successors.note: Cliopatria draws a separate Gascony to 1065; the William VIII page has the union in 1058 (the Duchy of Aquitaine page: personal union 'again from 1053'). The duchy survives as a title: the Duchy of Gascony page ends it in 1453.

capitals.name: Bordeaux
capitals.note: The infobox gives Bordeaux without years. Cliopatria's 768-824 shapes lie mostly south of the Pyrenees and do not reach Bordeaux; the seat of the Basque dukes 'of Bordeaux' (Seguin I, deposed 816) is the only ducal link the page names. Unverified by year.

rulers.name: Lop II
rulers.note: Page: 768/70-778/801; the 778 end is the Roncevaux year.

rulers.name: Seguin I Lop
rulers.note: Page: 812-816; 'Louis the Pious deposed the Basque Duke Seguin of Bordeaux' in 816.

rulers.name: Sans II Sancion
rulers.note: Page: 852-855/64; Arnaut (855/64) is a one-year entry left out. No duke is listed for 847-851.

rulers.name: Sans III Sancion (Mitarra)
rulers.note: 'appears to be the founder of a lineage' of independent dukes.

rulers.name: Sans VI Guilhem
rulers.note: Died in 1032; the page lists no duke for 1033-1051.

rulers.name: Gui-Geoffrey (William VIII of Aquitaine)
rulers.note: 'He became Duke of Gascony in 1052'; Duke of Aquitaine from 1058, after which Gascony is in union with Aquitaine.

keyframe_review.note: 55,717 km2 for 768-771, lat 42.0-44.8 across both sides of the Pyrenees: the Basque duchy at the moment of the Carolingian takeover ('768-769: The Carolingian takeover of Vasconia took place'; 'Lop II is the probable founder of a Gascon line of dukes'). The page gives no area. The page puts the duchy 'between the Garonne and the Adour' and the Pamplonese in it until 824; the shape is mostly the Basque country.
55,643 km2 (one-cell change from 768); nothing on the page for 772-777.

56,472 km2 for 778-782. The Roncevaux ambush of 15 August 778 ('The Frankish army's rearguard, led by Roland, was attacked by the Basque tribes') did not move the border; the Duchy page has Charlemagne 'begin[ning] appointing counts along the Garonne' that year. Cliopatria adds about 800 km2 that no page explains.

24,147 km2: the shape loses 129 cells north of the Pyrenees (-1.5 to 1.2 E, 42.8-44.7 N) when Louis is made king of Aquitaine in 781 ('It included not only Aquitaine proper, but also Gothia, Vasconia (Gascony)'); the kingdom-of-the-franks dossier records the same cells as its gain of 783. The remainder is the Basque country south of the Pyrenees, where 'In 781 two local Basque lords... were defeated and forced to submit' (Navarre page).
24,171 km2: 24 km2 more than 783; no page dates anything in 788-792.

16,199 km2: the east (lon 0.13 to 1.49, lat 42.04-42.30) leaves the shape. No page opened dates a change in 793; the loss is recorded at confidence 1 (the Franks' Spanish March is the neighbour). Left as drawn: unverified.

9,130 km2 for 806-824, the western Basque lands (lon -3.19 to -1.43, lat 42.56-43.41). The Navarre page: the Franks 'in 806 took Navarre under their protection'; the eastern part of the 793 shape leaves in that year (ledger loss 806). The shape ends with the detaching of the Pamplonese in 824.

correction.text: Gascony between the Garonne and the Pyrenees: the land of the independent Basque line from 864 ('The page places the duchy between the Garonne and the Adour')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a Cliopatria gap: no Gascony row exists for 825-989 although the page lists dukes in every generation and says 'Under the Basque line of dukes that began in 864, Gascony became effectively independent of the Frankish kings.' The shape from 864 is the 990 shape (Gascony between the Garonne and the Adour, 40,197 km2). For 825-863 the page shows Gascon dukes (Seguin II to 846, Sans II from 852) under Carolingian counts of Bordeaux, Toulouse and Fezensac and the Aquitanian sub-kings Pepin I and II; no land is drawn for them in this dossier.

40,197 km2 for 990-1017: Gascony north of the Pyrenees, 'between the Garonne and the Adour' with the counties of Béarn, Armagnac, Bigorre, Comminges, Nébouzan and Labourd 'that gained power as appanages'. The page gives no area; the Duchy of Aquitaine page says William V's duchy 'did not stretch south of the Garonne, a district which was in the possession of the Gascons'.
40,316 km2 (a few cells more than 990); the page dates nothing in 1018-1027.

40,174 km2: the same duchy; Sans VI Guilhem dies in 1032 and the protectorate of Sancho III of Pamplona over Gascony ('He also exerted a protectorate over the Duchy of Gascony', Navarre page, undated) is recorded in the Pamplona dossier as 1032-1035.

correction.text: the Gascon duchy unchanged, now under Gui-Geoffrey from 1052

keyframe_review.note: 40,316 km2 for 1046-1055. The shape holds to 1051; in 1052 'He became Duke of Gascony in 1052' (Gui-Geoffrey, who in 1058 became Duke of Aquitaine). 1052-1057 the duchy is Gui-Geoffrey's while his brother William VII holds Aquitaine, so the shape still stands for those years.

correction.text: the Gascon duchy for 1056-1057 only; from 1058 the same land is part of the Duchy of Aquitaine under William VIII

keyframe_review.note: 40,316 km2 for 1056-1065. Gui-Geoffrey 'ruled as Duke of Aquitaine and Count of Poitiers between 1058 and 1086, succeeding his brother William VII', which puts Gascony in personal union with Aquitaine from 1058 (the Duchy of Aquitaine page: 'again from 1053'). The shape holds for 1056-1057 only; from 1058 the land belongs to the Duchy of Aquitaine's colour and Cliopatria's 1058-1065 Gascony is superseded.

region.text: Vasconia, the Basque duchy on both sides of the western Pyrenees

ledger.note: 768: the Gascon line begins after the Carolingian takeover of Vasconia. 'c. 768-778/801: Lop II is the probable founder of a Gascon line of dukes'; '768-769: The Carolingian takeover of Vasconia took place'. Until then Gascony had been in personal union with Aquitaine (660-769 on the page); the Duchy of Aquitaine page: Waifer's 'assassination in 768 marked the demise of Aquitaine's relative independence', Frankish conquest 769.

region.text: Vasconia (Gascony) north of the Pyrenees, in Louis's kingdom of Aquitaine

ledger.note: 783: Gascony north of the Pyrenees passes to the Carolingian sub-kingdom. 'In 781, Charlemagne made his third son Louis, then three years of age, king of Aquitaine', a kingdom that 'included not only Aquitaine proper, but also Gothia, Vasconia (Gascony)'; the Gascon dukes remain (Sans I Lop, 778/801-812). Cliopatria moves the cells in 783; the Franks dossier has the same 129 cells as its gain.

region.text: the eastern edge of the Basque shape, by Cliopatria's drawing

ledger.note: 793: the east edge leaves the shape (bridging a silence). Cliopatria's Gascony drops from 24,171 to 16,199 km2 (lon 0.13 to 1.49 E, lat 42.04-42.30 N); the pages opened date nothing in 793, and name no taker. The Franks' Spanish March is the neighbour in the seed.

region.text: Navarre, which the Franks 'took under their protection'

ledger.note: 806: the Franks take Navarre under their protection. The Navarre page: the Franks 'in 806 took Navarre under their protection'; Cliopatria shrinks the Gascon shape from 16,199 to 9,130 km2 that year. The region is the part of the 793 shape that is not in the 806 shape, a reading of the page's 'Navarre'.

region.text: Gascony between the Garonne and the Pyrenees

ledger.note: 816: the Gascon revolt begins. 'Louis the Pious deposed the Basque Duke Seguin of Bordeaux', which 'started a widespread revolt led by García Jiménez'; the zone is Gascony proper, which the Franks hold since 783.

region.text: Gascony between the Garonne and the Pyrenees

ledger.note: 818: the revolt ends with its leader's death. The Navarre page: 'Garcia Jiménez, who led a Vasconic rebellion in Gascony against the Franks, was killed' in 818; the Duchy page lists Gassia I Semen (816-818) and Lop III Centullo Wasco (818-819/23) as the dukes of the time.

region.text: the Basque lands of the Pamplonese, now the Kingdom of Pamplona

ledger.note: 824: the Pamplonese leave the duchy. 'the definite detachment of Pamplona from the Duchy in 824'; 'the second Battle of Roncevaux took place' that year and the Navarre page has Íñigo Arista elected king of Pamplona in 824. Cliopatria's 806-824 shape is this land and ends here.

region.text: Gascony between the Garonne and the Adour

ledger.note: 864: Gascony is effectively independent under Sans III Sancion. 'Under the Basque line of dukes that began in 864, Gascony became effectively independent of the Frankish kings'; the Carolingian counts of Bordeaux, Toulouse and Fezensac had 'weakened the dukes' grip on power'. The land is Cliopatria's 990 shape (Garonne to Pyrenees); the page gives no boundary.

1052: Gui-Geoffrey of Poitiers becomes Duke of Gascony. 'He became Duke of Gascony in 1052 during his older brother William VII's rule'; the infobox names Bernard II Tumapaler as predecessor. The Aquitaine page adds that 'Odo or Eudes (d. 1039) joined Gascony to Aquitaine' and that the personal union dates 'again from 1053'. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Gascony, joined to Aquitaine under William VIII

ledger.note: 1058: Gui-Geoffrey becomes Duke of Aquitaine and Gascony joins the Duchy of Aquitaine. He ruled Aquitaine and Poitou 'between 1058 and 1086, succeeding his brother William VII'; the Aquitaine page has the union 'from 1053'. Cliopatria keeps a separate Gascony to 1065; the page does not say that the Duchy of Gascony ceased to exist as a title.
1058: the Gascon duchy merges into the Duchy of Aquitaine under William VIII; the land passes to the Duchy of Aquitaine's colour (the title survives to 1453 on the Duchy of Gascony page).

wars.name: Battle of Roncevaux Pass (778)
wars.outcome: Basque ambush of Charlemagne's rearguard on 15 August 778 ('led by Roland was attacked by the Basque tribes'); Pamplona's walls were destroyed in the retreat; no change of border.
wars.note: The Duchy page: 'Basques ambushed and slaughtered Charlemagne's rearguard' and Charlemagne 'also began appointing counts along the Garonne'.

wars.name: Gascon revolt of 816-818

zones.text: Gascony between the Garonne and the Pyrenees

wars.outcome: Louis the Pious deposed Seguin of Bordeaux (816), a revolt led by García Jiménez followed, and García was killed in 818.
wars.note: Not a Wikipedia article title; the Navarre page gives the 818 death.

wars.name: Battle of Roncevaux Pass (824)
wars.outcome: 'the second Battle of Roncevaux took place', Frankish counts Eblo and Aznar Galindo captured; the Pamplonese are 'definitively' detached from the duchy and Íñigo Arista is elected king of Pamplona.
wars.note: The Navarre page ties the ambush to 824 only through its linked title.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey draws any Gascon frontier in the pages opened; the page describes the duchy only as 'between the Garonne and the Adour'. The Pyrenean frontier with Pamplona (from 824) and the Garonne frontier with Aquitaine are approximate; 825-863 has no drawn land.

notes: Pages: 5 of 5 budgeted (the Kingdom of Aquitaine page returned the Duchy of Aquitaine text). Cliopatria rows: (1) the 768-824 shapes lie mostly south of the Pyrenees (lat 42.0-44.8 shrinking to a Basque strip of 9,130 km2 by 806) while the 990-1065 shapes are Gascony proper north of the Pyrenees; the two lives are different lands under one name. (2) No row for 825-989 although the page lists a duke in every generation; the dossier draws the 990 shape from 864 ('effectively independent') and nothing for 825-863, when the dukes sit under Carolingian counts. A gap-filler should open Gascon-specific pages (Seguin of Bordeaux, Sancho Mitarra) for 825-863. (3) 793 and 806 reductions: 793 unexplained (confidence 1); 806 read from the Navarre page's Frankish protection. End: the dossier ends in 1058, when Gui-Geoffrey (Duke of Gascony from 1052) became Duke of Aquitaine; Cliopatria keeps Gascony to 1065, and the Duchy of Aquitaine's Cliopatria shape presumably takes the land in 1066. The duchy-of-aquitaine dossier (eu-10) should carry the gain in 1058 or the orchestrator should move this end to 1065. The Duchy page gives the title's end as 1453 (annexed by France) and no date for the union with Aquitaine; the Aquitaine page gives 1039 (Odo) and 1053. Not settled: Gascony in 1032-1051 (no duke listed by the page, Bernard William and Bernard II Tumapaler are not on the pages opened beyond the infobox name); the protectorate of Sancho III (dated 1032-1035 in the Pamplona dossier; the Navarre page here has it undated). Counterparts: west-franks and duchy-of-aquitaine are other groups' dossiers; kingdom-of-pamplona exists. Region names used are Cliopatria shapes only, so there are no gazetteer gaps.
